title: YETI (YETI) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
transcript:
Margins expanded, but full-year sales guidance was trimmed.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

TAKEAWAYS

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email[email protected]

RISKS

SUMMARY

YETI Holdings, Inc.(YETI-10.49%)reported adjusted sales growth of 6% for the third quarter, supported by momentum in international markets and wholesale channels. Management adjusted the full year revenue and earnings outlook to account for a more cautious consumer spending environment and uneven demand trends observed in the United States and Canada. The company continued to execute on its Project Upcycle productivity initiative and maintained its capital allocation strategy through ongoing share repurchases. Despite near-term pressures in the Drinkware segment due to SKU concentration, the company reported expansion in adjusted gross and operating margins.

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator:Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the YETI Holdings Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results Conference Call.[Operator Instructions]This call is being recorded on Thursday, November 12, 2026. I would now like to turn the conference over to Arvind Bhatia, Head of Investor Relations at YETI. Please go ahead.

Arvind Bhatia:Good morning, and thank you for joining us to discuss YETI Holdings' Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 results. Leading the call today will be Matthew Reintjes, Chair of the Board and CEO; and Scott Bomar, CFO. Following our prepared remarks, we will open the call for your questions. Before we begin, we would like to remind you that some of the statements that we make today on this call may be considered forward-looking, and such forward-looking statements are subject to various risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from these statements. For more information, please refer to the risk factors detailed in our most recently filed Form 10-K.

We undertake no obligation to revise or update any forward-looking statements made today as a result of new information, future events or otherwise, except as required by law. Unless otherwise stated, our financial measures discussed on this call will be on a non-GAAP basis. We use non-GAAP measures in certain context as we believe they provide useful information regarding the underlying operating performance of our business. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures are included in the press release or in the presentation posted this morning to the Investor Relations section of our website at yeti.com. Please also refer to the supplemental information posted on the same website.

I would now like to turn the call over to Matt.

Matthew Reintjes:Thanks, Arvind, and good morning. We appreciate you all joining. YETI's third quarter results reflect the increasing breadth and balance of our global business and importantly, execution of our Built for the Wild strategy discussed at our recent Investor Day. Adjusted sales in the quarter grew more than 6%, led by Drinkware and International, with operating margins and EPS growth driving profit significantly faster than sales. And our free cash flow continued to fund both our long-term growth plans and additional share repurchases, bringing our total to $150 million year-to-date and $650 million since the beginning of our program in 2024.

Our performance reflects the multiyear work of our team and the consistent investments we have made in brand, innovation and global capabilities. What we laid out at Investor Day in September is coming to life across the business, a powerful, expanding global brand, a growing set of product platforms, a diversified omnichannel business and a financial model built to compound. That said, we want to be clear about the near-term demand pressure we're seeing, particularly in the U.S. and Canadian markets. Demand was uneven during Q3, and our current expectation is that it will remain pressured in the fourth quarter as we believe consumers are increasingly deal motivated.

Our cautious view of the near-term environment is appropriate right now, even as we have seen encouraging signals as our steady cadence of innovation continues to cut through a challenging promotional environment. In the fourth quarter, our focus is on quality growth and driving profitability. What has clearly not changed is our confidence in YETI's long-term opportunity. Our brand reads and reception to innovation continue to be positive and the diversity of our products, channels and geographies supported our execution this quarter and gives us more ways to win, setting us up for 2027 and in the quarters ahead. Scott will walk through the financials and our outlook in detail.

I'll focus on what we're seeing in the business, how our growth platforms are developing and why we're confident in where YETI is headed. I'll start with 4 key takeaways. First, the YETI brand continues to extend its reach and broaden its relevance while staying rooted. Our Four Letters brand campaign continues through targeted digital channels with a recent return to linear TV in Q4. As I mentioned in Q2, the campaign significantly expanded our reach and drove meaningful gains in brand search, consideration and ad recall. Just as important, the campaign strengthened how consumers connect YETI to their lifestyle. Those gains were broad-based, extending across younger consumers, women, sports fans and parents.

In Q3, we built on that momentum by tying Four Letters more directly to our products, our communities and consumers through targeted digital channels. In parallel with our overarching brand efforts, we're also focused on driving our community presence. We showed up across fishing, rodeo, surf, trail running, culinary and sports in the quarter, supported by our more than 200 ambassadors around the globe. You can see that connection across markets. The YETI Open, our annual public fishing event, generated more than 1.2 million impressions through event content. Boardmasters strengthened our position in British surf culture and turned brand energy into retail engagement across Europe.

In Australia and New Zealand, we built relevance at the national level through our partnerships with the All Blacks and Commonwealth Games Australia. Once again, the Calgary Stampede deepened our ties to Canada's outdoor and Western communities. And in Japan, our first Fuji Rock activation introduced YETI at an outdoor event with more than 120,000 attendees. We also extended our reach through partnerships and licensed products. We broadened our fandom collections across major professional and collegiate sports and signed our first professional soccer player, Michelle Cooper, who last weekend had a game winner in the quarterfinals of the NWSL Championship. This balance matters. Reach builds awareness, authenticity builds trust and YETI is delivering both.

These efforts are bringing new consumers to the brand, deepening engagement with existing ones and supporting growth across our product platforms, pursuits and geographies. We're also intentionally continuing a multi-quarter shift in marketing investment further up the funnel. That move can create some near-term transactional impact, but we believe it improves the quality of our revenue and the long-term value of our consumers. For holiday, we're building on that foundation with premium media, more targeted mid-funnel investment and a sharper focus on product discovery. When consumers are more deliberate about how they spend, brand strength matters. We see brand building as a compounding advantage, one that strengthens consumer connection today and expands the opportunity ahead.

Second, innovation continues to broaden our product platforms, giving consumers more reasons and more ways to engage with YETI. Q3 showed the breadth of that opportunity across soft coolers, bags, storage and protective cases, drinkware and cookware, products designed around clear needs in everyday use, giving us multiple avenues for growth. Soft coolers and bags remained important growth drivers. Daytrip led the expansion of our soft cooler platform with particularly strong year-to-date growth and building momentum internationally. Bags delivered strong growth led by Camino. The Camino Zip added functionality to an already successful franchise and drove incremental demand. And the Ranchero Crossbody exceeded our initial expectations for the bags portfolio.

Hard coolers, one of our core franchises, continues to perform well, while innovation is taking the category into new use cases. Tundra delivered strong performance in the quarter, a good reminder of the lasting relevance of one of our most iconic platforms. Smaller personal-sized hard coolers like the Roadie 8 and Roadie 15 are driving daily use and opening price points for YETI in the category. As you have seen, we're growing storage and protective cases through new GoBox sizes and accessories, and the LoadOut phone case brings YETI durability, design and performance into an entirely new everyday occasion.

That's how we think about innovation, build on the strength of our iconic franchises, extend successful platforms into new use cases, create entirely new reasons for consumers to engage with the brand. Drinkware is another example of that approach at work. While the category remains highly concentrated and competitive, stackable cups remain one of our strongest growth platforms and bottles and jugs are benefiting from everyday hydration demand. Hydration is a strategic priority with opportunity across quick access, leakproof, customizable and sport-related solutions. In the fourth quarter, we're building on those themes with the updated leakproof travel mug and additional ceramic-lined drinkware. The SKU concentrated pressure we outlined last quarter is playing out largely as expected.

It was an approximately 500 basis point impact to Drinkware growth in Q3 with similar pressure expected in Q4. Our full year expectation is unchanged at approximately 600 basis points to Drinkware. U.S. Drinkware wholesale inventory was down meaningfully on a 1- and 2-year stack as this category rotation continues as previously discussed. As those comparisons largely reset, we enter 2027 with a meaningfully more normalized base and a more diversified portfolio. Beyond Drinkware, we're extending YETI into more parts of consumers' daily lives. Food is gaining momentum as consumers build systems across bowls and Daytrip rather than buying individual products.

While early, cookware feedback has been strong as we look to further build upon that as an emerging growth platform. Taken together, our ability to turn consumer trust into new products, use cases and platforms is an important long-term advantage. In this environment, that breadth also gives us more ways to reach the consumer. Third, our omnichannel model is creating more ways for consumers to discover, experience and buy YETI. Wholesale was strong, reflecting retailer commitment to the brand. We continue to see opportunity for focused, impactful demand creation and product merchandising, some of which you will see this quarter at key wholesale partners. Our approach has not changed.

Productive distribution that elevates YETI's premium positioning, drives long-term shelf productivity and gives partners more opportunities to showcase the broadening portfolio. In D2C, traffic on our U.S. website remained pressured year-over-year as we comp Drinkware sales and Camino and Daytrip restocking last year. However, conversion improved and customer lifetime value increased. Amazon remains an important discovery and growth channel, though U.S. sales in the channel declined with the Prime Day shift from Q3 last year into Q2 this year, which had a greater impact than anticipated, particularly due to our reduced participation this year versus a year ago. B2B returned to strong growth, including in the U.S., driven by improving inbound demand, larger average order values and strength across platforms.

As we move across the fourth quarter, we are tracking consumer behavior closely in every channel. The diversity of our model gives us the flexibility to meet consumers wherever and however they choose to shop. During the holiday season, we can respond quickly as we see consumer behavior shift. Fourth, International momentum continues to prove that the YETI brand and playbook travel. International grew 19% in the quarter. Europe delivered a strong third quarter with growth across wholesale, digital and B2B. The U.K. was a standout, benefiting from wholesale growth, strong digital performance and rising brand awareness. On Amazon U.K., YETI reached the #1 position in coolers and #2 in drinkware.

Importantly, growth in the region is extending to more European markets beyond the U.K. That is exactly how we intend to build, grow awareness, establish premium distribution and connect with consumers through locally relevant communities and experiences. Asia, while still early, the progress is real. Japan remains a relatively small business, but sales grew significantly, led by e-commerce. In the past few weeks, we opened our first brand stores in Japan and Korea and launched our initial digital marketplace presence in China. Those are important steps in building our presence across the region, including in Korea and China, 2 of Asia's most important consumer markets. Australia and New Zealand delivered a very strong quarter led by wholesale and B2B.

Growth with key retail partners and momentum across product platforms reinforce the strength of the brand and the opportunity to keep scaling. In Canada, sales were down in a more challenging environment. We're building from a well-established brand foundation and continue to innovate as the Canadian market works through this softness. Customization and B2B performed particularly well, and innovation is giving consumers new reasons to engage. Additionally, our sports and community partnerships are also extending our reach with strong engagement across hockey, baseball and golf. The big picture internationally remains very compelling. We're growing established markets, building new ones and reaching consumers through more channels and more communities.

The playbook is disciplined and repeatable and it's working across very different markets. Turning to operations. As we scale, we continue to strengthen the capabilities behind the business. Our supply chain team expanded sourcing flexibility, strengthened logistics planning and added the operating capacity needed to support a broader portfolio and larger global footprint. Project Upcycle, our $100 million productivity program is gaining momentum with more than 50 active projects in the pipeline and meaningful wins already in the second half of 2026 that we expect will benefit 2027. We continue to diversify supply and expand our global development network with teams across the globe, building a connected innovation ecosystem that improves speed, testing, supplier collaboration and development capacity.

These investments are making YETI faster, more scalable and more productive. Stepping back, the quarter reinforced the strategy we laid out at Investor Day. Brand power compounds when reach is matched by innovation, creating more value as products become platforms and disciplined operations and capital allocation turn growth into durable shareholder returns. We have multiple paths for growth across categories, channels, geographies and consumers. Recent demand trends also remind us to stay agile and in a more challenging backdrop, drive productivity. So we're staying close to the consumer, focusing investment behind our strongest opportunities and managing the business with discipline. Taking a more cautious view of the near term does not mean pulling back.

We're staying on offense with brand, innovation and our evolving go-to-market while continuing to drive programs that underwrite increased profitability. Our fourth quarter priorities are clear; execute the holiday season. The long-term opportunity remains substantial. The brand is reaching more consumers, the portfolio is serving more needs and occasions, international markets are scaling and our operating model is becoming more capable and more efficient. While consumer and market conditions may fluctuate, the fundamentals of our business have not.

With a strong financial foundation, a powerful brand and increasingly diversified growth model, combined with the ability to expand margins and generate free cash flow, we believe YETI is well positioned to deliver sustained growth, attractive profitability and meaningful long-term value for our shareholders. I want to close by thanking our partners around the world and the entire YETI team. Q3 and our full year 2026 plan are a result of their work and reflect strong execution and a great foundation, setting YETI up for the long term. With that, I'll turn it over to Scott.

Scott Bomar:Thanks, Matt, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'll begin with our performance for the quarter, after which I'll provide an update on our outlook for 2026. We look forward to taking your questions following my prepared remarks. Before I get into the details, let me highlight a few of the most important themes from the quarter. We delivered another quarter of healthy growth with adjusted sales increasing 6% to approximately $518 million. Growth was broad-based across our major product categories and geographies, highlighted by an acceleration in Drinkware, continued momentum in our International business and strong growth in wholesale.

Profitability was also a significant highlight as adjusted gross margin expanded 310 basis points, and we generated operating leverage, driving adjusted operating income growth of 35% and adjusted EPS growth of 49%. We also continue to return capital to our shareholders, having now executed approximately $150 million in share repurchases for the year. Overall, we are pleased with the balance of growth and profitability we delivered in the quarter and importantly, the progress we continue to make in translating top line growth into faster earnings growth. During the quarter, we increased the reserve related to our 2023 product recalls. Our adjusted results exclude this reserve adjustment. Please refer to today's press release and our Investor Relations site for supplemental information.

With that, let's dive into the details. Third quarter adjusted sales increased 6% to approximately $518 million. Starting with our product categories. Drinkware adjusted sales increased 8% to $284 million. We are pleased to see growth in both the U.S. and international Drinkware, supported by strength within our core assortment and continued innovation. Coolers & Equipment adjusted sales increased 4% to $224 million, with contributions from our established cooler franchises as well as newer areas of the portfolio. The growth rate was in line with our expectations as we lapped last year's particularly strong demand and improved inventory for our highly successful soft coolers and bags extensions. Turning to our channels.

Wholesale sales increased 19% to approximately $237 million, with strong growth across the U.S., Europe and Australia. Direct-to-consumer adjusted sales declined 3% to approximately $281 million. Lower sales in our U.S.-owned e-commerce and Amazon Marketplace businesses were partially offset by growth internationally and in corporate sales. Results also included an unfavorable impact from the Prime Day shift from the third quarter last year to the second quarter this year. From a geographic perspective, U.S. adjusted sales increased 3% to approximately $399 million, with growth across both Coolers & Equipment and Drinkware. Our International business continued to grow at a significantly faster pace than the company overall, with sales increasing 19% to approximately $119 million.

Europe and Australia were key contributors to the growth, while we continue to expand the YETI brand in Japan. International represented 23% of adjusted sales compared with 21% in the prior year period. Taken together, our results reflect an increasingly diversified business with growth across both major product categories and geographies. Moving to gross margin. Adjusted gross profit increased 12% to approximately $305 million, while adjusted gross margin expanded 310 basis points to 59%. About 200 basis points of the improvement reflected lower net tariff costs. The remaining 110 basis points came from operating factors, including pricing and lower inbound freight, partially offset by higher product costs related to commodity inflation.

We are pleased with the magnitude of the year-over-year improvement and continued progress we are making across the underlying drivers of gross margin. Turning to SG&A. Adjusted SG&A increased 5% to approximately $215 million, with adjusted sales growing at a faster rate, adjusted SG&A improved 60 basis points as a percentage of adjusted sales to 41.6%. This leverage reflected the benefits of higher adjusted sales and ongoing productivity initiatives, while we continued investing in areas that support the long-term growth of the business. The combination of top line growth, gross margin expansion and SG&A leverage translated into a significant improvement in operating profitability.

Adjusted operating income increased 35% to $90 million, while adjusted operating margin expanded 370 basis points to 17.4% compared with 13.7% in the prior year period. We view this performance as another good illustration of the earnings power of our model and our ability to drive operating income growth meaningfully ahead of revenue growth. Moving to the bottom line. Adjusted net income increased 35% to approximately $67 million compared with approximately $50 million last year. Adjusted diluted EPS increased 49% to $0.91 compared with $0.61 in the third quarter of 2025. In addition to our operating performance, adjusted EPS benefited from the reduction in our share count as we continue to execute against our share repurchase authorization.

Turning to the balance sheet. We continue to maintain strong liquidity with approximately $74 million of cash and $71 million of total debt, excluding finance leases and unamortized deferred financing fees. Our $300 million revolving credit facility remained undrawn at quarter end. Inventory was approximately $394 million, up 22% from the prior year. The increase reflects the comparison against lower inventory levels a year ago, which were driven by supply constraints, new product launches as well as inventory built to support fourth quarter demand and future growth. With respect to cash flow, through the first 9 months of 2026, we generated approximately $110 million of cash from operating activities and approximately $72 million of free cash flow.

Our approach to capital allocation remains balanced between investing behind the long-term growth of YETI and returning excess capital to shareholders. During the third quarter, we repurchased approximately $20 million of shares, bringing total repurchases for the first 9 months of 2026 to approximately $150 million. We ended the quarter with approximately $350 million remaining under our share repurchase authorization. Now turning to our fiscal 2026 outlook. Before I get into the details, I want to note that we are returning to our historical practice of providing guidance on an adjusted basis to exclude 2023 product recall adjustments. Turning to our guidance.

We are updating our full year expectations to reflect a more cautious view of the consumer demand through the balance of the year. While we continue to see encouraging performance across several key areas of the business, demand has moderated in the early part of Q4. With the holiday season still ahead of us, we believe our revised outlook appropriately balances the underlying positives with the most recent demand trends we're seeing. We now expect full year adjusted sales growth of approximately 6% compared with our previous expectation of 7% to 8%. As a reminder, the prior year included a 53rd week, which created an estimated 100 basis point headwind to this year's growth rate.

Looking at the components of our adjusted sales outlook, we continue to expect Coolers & Equipment to grow high single to low double digits, including a return to double-digit growth in Q4. From a channel perspective, we continue to expect wholesale to grow high single to low double digits, while direct-to-consumer is expected to grow low single digits. Geographically, our updated outlook reflects moderated expectations across both the U.S. and international markets. We continue to expect the U.S. to grow low to mid-single digits, while we now expect International growth in the mid-teens compared to our prior outlook of high teens to 20%. The revision in the international outlook is driven primarily by a more cautious outlook for Canada.

Turning to profitability. We continue to expect healthy margin performance. We expect adjusted gross margin of approximately 57.5% to 58% for the year, unchanged from the prior outlook. This outlook incorporates our year-to-date performance resulting from operational drivers balanced against our current expectations for product costs and other margin drivers. For 2026, we expect the full year net tariff impact to be broadly consistent with 2025 levels. We expect adjusted operating expenses to increase approximately 5% to 7% for the full year. Given the softer demand environment, we remain focused on disciplined expense management while continuing to fund the investments that are important to YETI's long-term growth. Taken together, we expect adjusted operating income to increase approximately 7% to 9%.

We expect adjusted operating income margin of approximately 14.9%, which is unchanged from our prior guidance. Turning to the remaining P&L items in our guidance. We expect an effective tax rate of approximately 24% and diluted weighted average shares outstanding of approximately 75.1 million. We now expect adjusted earnings per diluted share of approximately $2.90 to $2.95, representing growth of approximately 16% to 18% compared with 2025. We continue to expect capital expenditures between $60 million and $70 million and free cash flow between $200 million and $225 million in 2026. Looking ahead, our confidence in YETI's long-term opportunity has not changed.

As we outlined at Investor Day, we believe we have substantial runway ahead, supported by a durable brand, a proven innovation engine, an increasingly global business and an operating model designed to scale. We are still early in realizing that potential with opportunities to expand into new categories and use cases, build bags and soft coolers into a much larger platform and extend YETI's reach across international markets. The opportunity is not limited to the top line. Project Upcycle is designed to help offset macro cost pressures, create capacity to invest in the business and support sustainable margin expansion. Together, these growth and productivity initiatives underpin the long-term financial framework that we shared at Investor Day.

So while we are taking a more cautious view of the near-term consumer environment, it does not change our conviction in the long-term potential of this business. We are focused on executing with discipline, continuing to invest in high-return opportunities and positioning YETI to deliver durable, profitable growth and sustainable value for our shareholders. With that, I'll turn the call back over to the operator.

Operator:[Operator Instructions]Your first question comes from Peter Keith from Piper Sandler.

Peter Keith:I guess I want to dig in first on the DTC weakness. It's a bit surprising to me coming off the heels of the Four Letters brand campaign, and you have been citing increased search activity. But you're also highlighting a consumer that is more deal motivated. So I'm wondering, do you think you might be pivoting to a bit more promotional cadence as we go into the holiday? And related on that, given the Q4 sales outlook, should we expect DTC to be negative again in Q4?

Matthew Reintjes:Peter, thanks for the question. I would say a couple of things. As we talked about at our Investor Day, and we've continued to believe the power of our go-to-market and that omnichannel approach and the importance of our wholesale partnerships and the various elements of our D2C. In Q3, we had some dynamics. The Amazon Prime shift from Q3 to Q2 was a significant shift for us. As we talked about the traffic in our dot-com in Q3, which was really a rollover of the restocking efforts in Camino and the Daytrip soft coolers last year.

And then this dynamic we've talked a lot about, which is the concentrated Drinkware SKUs and the trend in those and the pressure in the quarter and the pressure on the year. So when we look at all those dynamics, our commercial go-to-market, our omnichannel approach, the power of the way we go to market, we think, continues to be a competitive advantage. And when we study our owners, what we see is that just under half of our owners shop 3-plus channels that we operate in and almost 3/4 plus shop at least 2 channels. So that power of the omnichannel is incredibly important. It doesn't mean we prioritize one over the other.

We're really trying to drive the overall impact to go chase all the unmet demand that we continue to believe still sticks out there for YETI.

Scott Bomar:Just a couple of add-ons. If you exclude the impact from the Prime Day shift, DTC would have been approximately flat in Q3. And as it relates to Q4, we do expect to see positive growth in DTC in Q4.

Peter Keith:Okay. All right. That's good. Maybe just looking forward, I guess the implied guide for Q4 would have sales growth below the long-term sales algo of mid- to high single digits. As you look forward to '27, I know you're not guiding next year, do you see opportunities to get back up to that mid- to high single-digit algo target?

Scott Bomar:Yes. Thanks for the question. Look, we're not seeing anything that makes us feel differently about 2027 than we did during Investor Day. We're early in the process and are working through our planning cadences to prepare for [indiscernible] guidance. We're not doing that today. But we do expect it to be within our long-term algo. As a reminder, Q4 did have a 53rd week a year ago. If you adjust for that, that's 300 basis points. So we're not far off the algo even in Q4 with the revised expectations that we've put out there today. When we look at this, we say our core franchises just continue to perform well. We've got a robust innovation pipeline.

We don't have some of the pressures that we talked about. There's no 53rd week in 2027. We don't have the pressure from these trend-driven SKUs that we've talked about. So we feel like broadly the backdrop is constructive for 2027. We are seeing continued cost pressures related to inflationary pieces like things like resins, stainless steel, magnets, fuel prices are weighing on our transportation costs. But we're not standing still. We've got Project Upcycle, as Matt referenced in his comments, that's delivering real returns, and we're working through the cost pressures and starting to see some terrific results from our initiatives to change the cost structure of this business going forward.

So broadly speaking, we expect to be within the long-term algo as we come out with 2027 expectations.

Operator:Your next question comes from Randy Konik from Jefferies.

Randal Konik:Just on the -- back to the long-term algo. Scott, as we think about next year, can you just give us maybe some of the puts and takes on the top line in terms of how we should be thinking about that mid- to high single-digit range? Just curious on different launches that are coming through, geographies that are being expanded upon or getting deeper in terms of distribution? Just give us some of the puts and takes that we should be thinking about next year as we think about just modeling within that mid- to high single-digit framework.

Scott Bomar:Sure. Yes. Maybe I'll just start with a couple of things that are related to the absence of headwinds. The absence of headwinds is -- there's no 53rd week comparison. There's no -- the trend-driven SKUs we brought up a number of times in the last couple of quarters, that essentially goes to 0 starting in Q1. So that pressure subsides. And then our innovation pipeline is robust. You saw a little bit of that. We gave you a teaser on some of the things that we're bringing out in 2027 during the Investor Day. We see continued efforts to optimize and refine and enhance our commercialization strategies.

We've had terrific results in Europe and Asia and some of the early launches there. We're seeing terrific results from our investments in those markets. And so we think on balance, again, the diversity of the business model, where we expect to see progress across channel and product categories. We feel like we're well positioned for 2027. And again, I think in spite of the unevenness we've seen in customer demand in the last month or so, we expect to have a constructive backdrop for 2027.

Randal Konik:Great. And then maybe the same kind of puts and takes type question as it pertains to thinking again over into '27 for the margin side of the ledger in terms of -- you talked about some headwinds on resin pricing and so on and so forth, but there seems to be other items in terms of -- on the SG&A line, for example, with Project Upcycle. So maybe kind of give us again how we should be thinking about puts and takes as it pertains to margins as we get past the fourth quarter and into next year as well?

Scott Bomar:Yes, sure. Thanks, Randy. Look, nothing's really changed meaningfully quarter-over-quarter as it relates to the pressures that we're seeing. It's the same things we talked about before. It's fuel and fuel-related inputs, whether they affect the price of resins that move -- they're part of plastics, stainless steel, fuel more directly as it relates to our transportation cost. So those haven't meaningfully changed quarter-over-quarter. We had sort of a partial year impact from that in 2026, and we'll see that wrap around in 2027. Although, look, we're sitting here in November. Back half of next year is quite a ways away, and so we'll see how that plays out over time. Let me spend a quick second on tariffs.

I think this is an important one to clarify. Tariffs in 2025, as we've talked about a number of times, were approximately $40 million in the P&L. That was sort of a half year convention, where we had roughly 20% tariffs affecting roughly half the year in 2025, which is about $40 million. We had a number of changes, as you've all followed very carefully, over the course of 2026, including the refunds, a change in the expectations about the base tariff rates. All in 2026 tariff impact is approximately $40 million as well. And so year-over-year, the tariff impact to '26 versus '25 is effectively 0, approximately 0.

And so when we highlight full year expectations of 16% to 18% earnings per share growth, essentially, that's tariff neutral. That reflects the operating power, the operating model and the economic engine of YETI. And so that I think it's important to be clear about that. As that rolls forward into 2027, there will be a little bit of overhang on tariffs because in the early part of the year, effectively, there were no tariffs realized in the P&L in January and February as the 122 tariffs didn't come into place until late February. So as far as an overhang as it relates to cost, there will be a little bit of additional tariff pressure.

That said, we continue to work hard. Project Upcycle, it continues to deliver success. We have 50 active projects, a few early wins. The benefit from that effort isn't going to happen all at once. It's going to take time. But we're really excited about the momentum that the team is building there and the impact that can have on the P&L over the long haul.

Operator:Your next question comes from Phillip Blee from William Blair.

Olivia May Witte:This is Olivia Witte on for Phillip Blee. So I guess for the softness in the domestic direct channel, do you think there's any correlation with consumers increasingly using AI as a product discovery tool and traditional search marketing becoming less effective? Or are you seeing anything across your own site or Amazon that suggests the weakness is driven more by general consumer and macro pressures? And have you seen any meaningful change in customer acquisition costs, site traffic or conversion that would help distinguish between those factors?

Matthew Reintjes:Olivia, thanks for the question. Obviously, that's something we pay a lot of attention to, and we've talked a little bit about in the past of our efforts to make sure that we are showing up really well, which we believe we do today in the off-platform search in the various models. And some of that is the richness of the content we create, some of it's the changes we continue to make to our website to make sure that it shows up and our products show up well in those searches.
